title: Total-tensor and K-flat representative comparison for ringed slice extension
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small Grothendieck site, let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and let $U$ be an object of $\mathcal C$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use the localized ringed site $(\mathcal C/U,R_U)$ with exact restriction $j^*$, and the exact module extension $j_!$ left adjoint to it [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. For any unbounded cochain complex $P$ of $R_U$-module sheaves and any unbounded cochain complex $C$ of $R$-module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], the sheaf tensor isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor] induce a natural chain isomorphism
$$\Phi_{P,C}:j_!\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_{R_U}j^*C)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}(j_!P\otimes_R C).$$
Here $j_!$ and $j^*$ act termwise and total tensor uses direct sums in each total degree and differential $d_P\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_C$ on the $(p,q)$ summand [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. The component of $\Phi$ on that summand is the indicated sheaf tensor isomorphism and the coproduct insertion; it is natural in both chain maps. If $P$ is K-flat over $R_U$, then $j_!P$ is K-flat over $R$. If $P\to H$ is a K-flat resolution, then $j_!P\to j_!H$ is a K-flat resolution [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Neither boundedness nor a constant-ring hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0E8I (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor), extended to unbounded direct-sum total complexes; K-flatness by the acyclic tensor test. Agent-formulated representative refinement of the sheaf lemma.

proof.text: Write $T^{p,q}=P^p\otimes_{R_U}j^*C^q$. The adjunction $j_!\dashv j^*$ of [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] show that the canonical map $\bigoplus_{p+q=n}j_!T^{p,q}\longrightarrow j_!(\bigoplus_{p+q=n}T^{p,q})$ is invertible. The index is the small discrete set $\{(p,q)\in\mathbf Z^2:p+q=n\}$. Direct sums exist by [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Compose its inverse with the direct sum of the natural sheaf isomorphisms $\theta_{p,q}:j_!T^{p,q}\xrightarrow{\sim}(j_!P^p)\otimes_R C^q$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor]. This defines an isomorphism $\Phi^n$ in each degree. In particular, $\Phi^n\circ j_!(\iota_{p,q})=\iota_{p,q}\circ\theta_{p,q}$, with the target insertion into its total degree.

source.place: Tag 0E8I (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor); categories.tex Tag 0038 (lemma-adjoint-exact), applied to the direct sums of Homology Tag 012Z

proof.text: Let $J=j_!$. Naturality of $\theta$ in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor], first for $(d_P^p,1)$ and then for $(1,d_C^q)$, gives $\theta_{p+1,q}J(d_P^p\otimes1)=(Jd_P^p\otimes1)\theta_{p,q}$ and $\theta_{p,q+1}J(1\otimes j^*d_C^q)=(1\otimes d_C^q)\theta_{p,q}$. Since the functors are additive by their exactness [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], they preserve the sign $(-1)^p$. Add the two equations and insert into total degree $n+1$ using the differential formula of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. The result on every summand is $d\Phi^nJ(\iota_{p,q})=\Phi^{n+1}J(d)J(\iota_{p,q})$; these maps determine a map out of the coproduct from step 1. Thus $\Phi$ is a chain isomorphism. Replacing the two differentials in the same naturality equations by the components of arbitrary chain maps proves naturality in both variables. No infinite sum of maps into a fixed summand is used: each source summand has only the two specified differential components.

source.place: Tag 012Z (definition-associated-simple-complex); sites-modules.tex Tag 0E8I, naturality of the sheaf tensor comparison

proof.text: We will use the tensor factors in the order of the K-flatness test. For any two complexes $A,B$, the sectionwise map $x\otimes y\mapsto y\otimes x$ is balanced over the commutative coefficient ring and has itself as inverse. It respects restrictions, so sheafification gives the ordinary tensor symmetry [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. On total complexes define $\tau_{A,B}$ on the $(a,b)$ summand by $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{ab}y\otimes x$ into the $(b,a)$ summand [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. The coefficient of $d_By\otimes x$ in both $d\tau$ and $\tau d$ is $(-1)^{ab}$, because $a+a(b+1)\equiv ab\pmod2$; that of $y\otimes d_Ax$ is $(-1)^{ab+b}=(-1)^{(a+1)b}$. Hence this is a chain map and $\tau_{B,A}\tau_{A,B}=1$. The direct sum universal property makes this a chain isomorphism without boundedness assumptions.

source.place: Tag 012Z (definition-associated-simple-complex), explicit signed interchange; sites-modules.tex Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product)

proof.text: Suppose $P$ is K-flat, and let $C$ be any acyclic complex of $R$-modules. By exactness of restriction [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] and the homology comparison in clause (c) of [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology], $H^n(j^*C)\cong j^*H^n(C)=0$. Thus $\operatorname{Tot}(j^*C\otimes_{R_U}P)$ is acyclic by [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Step 3 identifies it with $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_{R_U}j^*C)$. Exactness of $j_!$ and the same homology comparison show that applying $j_!$ termwise keeps it acyclic. Steps 1 and 2 identify the result with $\operatorname{Tot}(j_!P\otimes_R C)$, and step 3 identifies this with $\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes_R j_!P)$. Consequently the latter is acyclic for every acyclic $C$, exactly the assertion that $j_!P$ is K-flat. Exact functors send zero objects to zero objects, so each displayed zero follows from the cited homology comparison.

Let $f:P\to H$ be a K-flat resolution, hence a quasi-isomorphism with $P$ K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. The natural homology comparison of [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology], applied to the exact functor $j_!$ of [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], identifies $H^n(j_!f)$ with $j_!H^n(f)$. The latter is invertible since a functor preserves isomorphisms. Thus $j_!f$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and step 4 makes its source K-flat; it is a K-flat resolution of $j_!H$. All arguments use the localized ring sheaf $R_U$ and countable coproducts, so no constant-coefficient or boundedness hypothesis has entered.
